transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Srinivasan (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Carlos Diaz (StellarNet), Aisha Khan (StellarNet), Mark Tan (StellarNet), Renee Wu (StellarNet)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick sync to align on marketplace listing and RA, some background on StellarNet requirements, discuss security & KMS, agree on deliverables.

[00:00] Morgan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm morgan from redwood, quick roll call?
[00:06] Carlos Diaz: carlos here, hey, and excited to move this along
[00:09] Priya Srinivasan: priya here from se, i'll lead on the RA draft and technical parts
[00:13] Aisha Khan: aisha, platform eng, i'll own the network side
[00:17] Mark Tan: mark - security, will be looking at KMS and compliance
[00:21] Evan Cho: evan from solutions, i'll run the integration tests and sample flows
[00:25] Renee Wu: renee product - ok to take notes on product expectations

[02:00] Morgan Lee: high level agenda, we want to cover marketplace tile requirements, the reference architecture for private/VPC deployments, auth and key mgmt, and then timeline and next steps. does that look right?
[02:18] Carlos Diaz: yes that's right. our partnership team wants a clean listing in the marketplace and also a joint RA so our customers can deploy quickly.

[04:10] Priya Srinivasan: i'll start with marketplace listing - typically we need a tile json (manifest) with screenshots, a short blurb, quickstart steps, supported regions and pricing model. we also have a validation checklist for the marketplace - things like health check endpoints, version pinning, support contact.
[04:33] Aisha Khan: are there specific network requirements for the tile or is that part of the RA?
[04:38] Priya Srinivasan: good question, a bit of both - the tile can list recommended network ports and peering options but the RA will show the detailed vpc architecture, peering, nat/gateway, and security groups.

[06:20] Evan Cho: real quick note - for private deployments we often recommend a customer-managed control plane on a bastion with redwood agents in the VPC, or a fully managed VPC link for customers that want us to operate. staging will need KV cache warmup and sample workloads to validate latency numbers.
[06:45] Mark Tan: when you say bastion + agents, is that relying on SSH access or some sort of mutual TLS?
[06:52] Priya Srinivasan: we use mTLS between agents and the control plane, SSH only for admin debug with explicit auditing; hope that's fine, we can include those details in the RA.

[09:12] Carlos Diaz: on billing/marketplace side, stellarnet has its own billing connector; how does redwood expect to expose metering for per-token usage or reserved capacity?
[09:26] Morgan Lee: two options: export usage events via webhook to your billing system, or use marketplace metering APIs - we support both. for dedicated/reserved we also surface committed capacity tags so marketplace tile can show committed tiers.
[09:45] Renee Wu: can we show both hosted api and dedicated options on the same tile? customers want to choose.
[09:51] Priya Srinivasan: yes the tile can enumerate variants; we usually list featured deployment modes and link to docs for tradeoffs - e.g., latency vs cost.

[12:05] Aisha Khan: security - we need specifics on encryption at rest and key management. do you integrate with external KMS?
[12:13] Priya Srinivasan: we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can support HSMs for enterprise - our control plane stores metadata only, secrets are in KMS and never in clear. we'll share the security whitepaper.
[12:33] Mark Tan: and do you have an attestation or key rotation process?
[12:37] Evan Cho: yes rotation supported, we have automated rotation windows and support bring-your-own-key with rotation hooks. we'll include rotation runbook in the RA.

[15:02] Carlos Diaz: network policies: our customers in regulated industries require no egress except to certain endpoints - can the marketplace listing indicate allowed endpoints and a minimal set?
[15:14] Priya Srinivasan: absolutely, RA will include a minimal outbound allowlist and optional proxying patterns for restricted environments.

[17:30] Morgan Lee: a bit on QA - our marketplace QA requires a demo flow with health checks, sample requests, and a rollout plan for upgrades. evan will prepare a test plan.
[17:44] Evan Cho: plan will include smoke tests for generation endpoints, load test script for 100 qps, and a KV cache warmup scenario. we'll also provide a docker-compose for local sanity testing.

[20:00] Aisha Khan: one of our customers uses private on-prem clusters, any gotchas for on-prem shipping?
[20:10] Priya Srinivasan: on-prem mostly comes down to network/firewall rules and hardware compatibility - quantization profiles can vary by GPU. we'll document recommended instance SKUs and minimum memory for model variants.

[22:55] Carlos Diaz: who owns the reference architecture doc? is that redwood or joint?
[23:02] Morgan Lee: we usually draft the initial RA (redwood SEs) and then make it joint - we'll include StellarNet logos and call out partner-specific notes where you provide topology and environment constraints.

[25:40] Mark Tan: compliance notes - SOC2 and ISO - we need the exact sections to reference in our procurement.
[25:48] Priya Srinivasan: we'll attach a SOC2 summary and list of controls; for anything deeper we can sign an NDA and share more detailed reports.

[28:30] Renee Wu: on the marketplace product listing copy - is there a preferred length and do you have brand guidelines for the tile image?
[28:38] Morgan Lee: short blurb ~50-100 words, one hero image (1200x600) and 3 screenshots, and links to quickstart and docs. we'll share the tile spec and a template.

[30:11] Carlos Diaz: timeline expectation - stellarnet would like a live tile within 6 weeks if possible, with RA ready in 2 weeks. realistic?
[30:22] Priya Srinivasan: 2 weeks for RA draft is realistic; marketplace listing depends on QA cycles - 4-6 weeks is reasonable if we schedule QA early.

[33:05] Evan Cho: technical detail - for model variants and pinning we recommend explicit model tags; the tile and RA should specify compatible model versions and quantization profiles per deployment target.
[33:20] Aisha Khan: ok can you give an example of a model tag format so our infra team can map?
[33:25] Priya Srinivasan: e.g., redwood/gpt-3.8-q4f16:20260401, we'll add that to the sample manifest.

[36:00] Mark Tan: incident response - if there's a security event, what's the escalation path?
[36:07] Morgan Lee: we have an incident runbook, and enterprise customers get a 24/7 pager and designated account contacts; we'll include the contact list and SLAs in the partnership appendix.

[38:40] Carlos Diaz: marketplace approval often flags data residency - do you support region locking?
[38:46] Priya Srinivasan: yes, our platform can restrict model serving to specific regions and we expose region selectors in the tile. for private deployments it's obviously customer-controlled.

[40:50] Renee Wu: commercial - do you need to surface Redwood pricing or will stellarnet bill customers fully?
[40:57] Morgan Lee: flexible - you can resell or refer; for resell we provide metering hooks and a revenue share model. legal will follow up with contract language.

[43:15] Aisha Khan: any pre-built terraform modules or helm charts we can include in the RA?
[43:23] Evan Cho: yes we have terraform modules for peering, secrets, and a helm chart for agent deployment; we'll attach examples to the RA repo.

[45:00] Morgan Lee: ok let's recap action items and owners - priya will draft RA, evan will draft test plan, morgan will send tile spec and whitepaper, aisha/stellarnet to share network topology and compliance list.
[45:20] Carlos Diaz: sounds good, will drive internal stakeholders and get topology over.

[47:32] Renee Wu: quick question on integrations - are there any hard blockers we should be aware of?
[47:38] Priya Srinivasan: not really, only typical infra gaps - if your customers want air-gapped on-prem we may need additional validation for models and quantization, but it's all doable.

[49:10] Morgan Lee: awesome, next sync after RA draft review - propose 2026-04-28 for a 30-minute follow up.
[49:22] Carlos Diaz: ok we'll take that. thanks everyone.
[49:28] Morgan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links. bye.

End of transcript.
